Chapter 9: Bringing the Story Home—Applying the Lessons in Daily Life.
You know, stories have this incredible power to move us. But their real magic? It shows up in what we actually do with them.
As the friends wrapped up their conversation, something shifted. Suddenly, the maze and the cheese weren’t just part of a fable—they started to see their own lives reflected in that story. For them, the tale became a kind of mirror, showing their struggles, their hopes, and maybe even their blind spots.
One friend, feeling inspired, decided it was finally time to chase a new career. She realized waiting around for the “old cheese” to come back was only holding her back. Another friend made a tough decision too—he was ready to have that difficult conversation with a family member, because clinging to old habits was keeping both of them stuck.
And then there was the third friend. Change had always felt scary, but now he promised himself to try something new every single week, even if it was just a small step.
They all agreed to check in with each other, to share their own “writings on the wall” as they faced new challenges. Suddenly, the story gave them a shared language—a way to talk about change without feeling afraid or embarrassed.
Here’s something you might find interesting: the lessons from the maze aren’t just for big, dramatic life changes. They fit right into the everyday—like picking up a new hobby, reaching out to a new friend, letting go of a grudge, or just opening your mind to a fresh idea.
The friends realized that, while change can shake you up, it can also bring growth and new beginnings. And by facing it together, they felt less alone—and a whole lot more hopeful about what’s ahead.
